title: Meningococcal vaccine
what: A vaccine shot that protects against meningococcus, a bacterium that can cause meningitis and blood infection.
why: For children and teens when advised, students living in dormitories, before pilgrimage and travel, and with some illnesses.
duration: the shot takes a few seconds; with the check-up usually 15 to 40 minutes
tell_doctor: If you are sick now or have a fever
Allergies and strong reactions to past vaccines
If you have no spleen or have immune problems
Where you plan to travel, as the vaccine is required for some countries

prepare.title: Health
prepare.text: The vaccine is given when you are healthy. You will be examined before the shot.

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: Before a trip, the vaccine is usually given in advance, at least 10 days. Ask your doctor.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes so the shoulder is easy to uncover.

steps: A doctor or nurse asks how you feel and takes your temperature
The skin is wiped and the shot is given
The vaccine is recorded in the documents
After the shot, sit at the clinic for about 30 minutes
feel: Sometimes the spot aches for 1 to 2 days
Sometimes headache, weakness or a mild fever
after: Stay near the office for 30 minutes
You can go back to your usual activities
The doctor will say whether a booster is needed
red_flags: Trouble breathing, swelling of the face or throat, a rash all over: call your local emergency number

faq.q: How long does the vaccine last?
faq.a: It depends on the vaccine and age. Sometimes a booster is needed. Ask your doctor.

faq.q: Is it needed before Hajj or Umrah?
faq.a: Usually yes, it is required. Check the requirements in advance and keep the certificate.

reminders.text: Meningococcal vaccine tomorrow. Bring your ID and vaccination record.
